title: Natural Writing
description: Rewrite tickets, docs, PR text, and code comments so wording sounds human, not AI jargon. A durable avoid-list grows from feedback.
triggers: drafting a message for someone else

inputs.text: string (optional) — an existing draft to rewrite; if omitted, applies while drafting new prose

guarantees: Before presenting any prose written for other people to read (Jira tickets, documentation, PR/commit descriptions, code comments, chat/Slack messages), checks it against avoid-list.md in this skill directory and rewrites a listed term when it's a reflexive or overused choice — not a hard ban, so a listed term stays when it's genuinely the most accurate or natural word for that spot.
Beyond exact list matches, flags corporate-jargon vocabulary and stock AI phrasing on judgment — technically accurate words that no colleague would actually say out loud.

When the user flags a specific word, phrase, or construction as sounding unnatural or AI-generated, appends a new row to avoid-list.md (the flagged term, a plain alternative, and dated context) before continuing the current task — never asks permission first.
Only swaps register and vocabulary; never changes technical meaning or drops a term that has no natural plain-English substitute.
Applies only to output meant for other humans — not to internal reasoning, code identifiers, or established domain terms.
non_goals: Does not handle sentence-level structure, em dashes, or prepositional compression — already covered by the global Writing Style rules in CLAUDE.md.
Does not remove precise technical terms, API names, flags, or established jargon with no natural substitute.
Does not shorten or drop content to sound more casual — that's a compression concern, not a word-choice one.
Does not restructure documentation for discoverability — that's docs-writing.
Does not treat avoid-list.md as a banned-word list — a listed term used sparingly, and genuinely the best fit for what's being said, is left in place.
notes: See CLAUDE.md in this skill directory for the full checking and feedback-logging procedure, and avoid-list.md for the living, feedback-built list of flagged terms — the actual artifact this skill's self-improvement writes to.
